task_text: Clear the blocker, recover and bank into the goal: A square puck slides toward the robot over an almost frictionless table at the start. First touch it with the paddle; then strike it so that, sliding free of the paddle, it hits a sliding blocker bar that obstructs the way to the goal fast enough to push it aside along its rail. Let the puck slide back across a recovery line by itself, strike it a second time, and make it bank off the rail designated for this episode (one of two rails, coloured green; the other is grey) without touching the other rail, and then cross the goal line while the blocker is still pushed aside. Phases, in order: first_strike: the puck touches the paddle.; clear_blocker: the puck, sliding free of the paddle, hits the blocker fast enough and pushes it aside. The free time is the time since the puck last touched the paddle. During this phase a puck-blocker contact with a free time below `strike_free` = 0.15 s fails the task (puck_pushed_into_blocker). A contact with a free time of at least 0.15 s while the puck's horizontal speed on the previous physics step was at least `strike_min_speed` = 0.15 m/s counts as the hit; a slower contact counts for nothing. The phase completes at the first step at which the hit has happened and the blocker is displaced more than 0.065 m along its rail from its start (joint position q > 0.065 m).; recover_deflection: the puck's centre crosses the recovery line x = 0.16 m toward the robot (x >= 0.16 on one physics step and < 0.16 on the next) while it does not touch the paddle and has not touched it for at least `recover_free` = 0.15 s: it must come back by itself.; second_strike: the puck touches the paddle again.; bank_and_goal: after its last paddle contact the puck must bank off the designated rail (see Goal geometry), touch no other rail, and then cross the goal line. A bank is the onset of a contact with the designated rail (a step with that contact after a step without it) at least `bank_free` = 0.1 s after the puck's last paddle contact. Every paddle contact starts a new attempt: it clears an earlier bank and an earlier contact with the other rail. The phase completes when the puck's centre crosses the goal line, world x = 0.46 m, moving in +x (x <= 0.46 on one physics step and > 0.46 on the next) with |y - 0.06| < 0.055 m (y between 0.005 and 0.115 m), while a bank has been made since the last paddle contact, the puck has not touched the other rail since that contact, it does not touch the paddle, and the blocker is still displaced more than 0.065 m. This completes the task. A crossing of that segment in this phase without all of these fails the task: wrong_rail when the puck has touched the other rail since its last paddle contact, skipped_route otherwise. Goal geometry: At this instance the designated rail is the short end rail on the robot's side of the play area (coloured green): the final shot must bank off it, without touching the long side rail on the robot's right, before it crosses the goal line. Goal line: world x = 0.46 m for 0.005 m < y < 0.115 m (centre (0.46, 0.06), half-width 0.055 m), to be crossed in +x. Recovery line: world x = 0.16 m, crossed toward -x (recover_deflection).
episode: one episode, no reset: it ends at the first control step where the task has succeeded (every phase in order) or failed (a failure event, a forbidden contact, a safety-limit violation, an object out of bounds, or the task's horizon of 35 s of simulated time, 3500 control steps), when your time is up, or on a simulator error; the simulated clock advances only with the control steps you run
